governance.title: Radix Governance: proposals, temperature checks and votes
governance.description: Every Radix community proposal and temperature check read from the ledger: status, XRD results, quorum and voting with your Radix Wallet.

governance.hero_subtitle: Every community proposal and temperature check, read straight from the Radix ledger. See how they are going, what was decided and vote with your Radix Wallet.

how_steps.title: 1. Temperature check
how_steps.text: Anyone can raise an idea. The community votes for or against to gauge support before going further.

how_steps.title: 2. Formal proposal
how_steps.text: If the temperature check passes, it becomes a formal proposal with its ballot options, its quorum and the share it needs to pass.

how_steps.title: 3. Result
how_steps.text: Each account votes with the voting power it held when voting opened. If enough XRD takes part and the threshold is met, it passes.

detail_hints.system: Governance system running this vote: who organises it, publishes the tally and carries out the result. The link opens its official website.
detail_hints.kind_proposal: Formal proposal: the vote that decides a specific change. It usually follows a temperature check that gathered enough support.
detail_hints.kind_temperature_check: Temperature check: a non-binding vote to gauge community support for an idea before it becomes a formal proposal.
detail_hints.number: This vote's number within its system. Proposals and temperature checks are numbered separately.
detail_hints.parameters: Set of rules the vote was created with. It sets the quorum, the approval threshold and the duration that apply to it.
detail_hints.quorum: Minimum voting power, in XRD, that must take part for the result to be valid. If it is not reached, the vote does not count, whichever option wins.
detail_hints.threshold: Share of the votes in favour, out of votes in favour and against, needed to pass. Abstentions do not count.
detail_hints.max_options: How many options each voter may pick on their ballot.
detail_hints.duration: How long the vote stays open, from opening to closing.
detail_hints.starts: Opening date and time. Each account's voting power is taken from its balances at this moment, so buying XRD afterwards adds no votes.
detail_hints.ends: Closing date and time. From then on no votes are accepted and the result is final.
detail_hints.voters: Distinct addresses that have voted. If one changed its mind, only its latest vote counts.
detail_hints.author_proposal: Account that created this proposal on the ledger. Click to see its activity in the explorer.
detail_hints.author_temperature_check: Account that raised this temperature check on the ledger. Click to see its activity in the explorer.
detail_hints.component: Address of the component (the Radix smart contract) that stores this system's votes. Everything shown here is read straight from it.
detail_hints.from_tc: Temperature check this formal proposal came from.
detail_hints.to_proposal: Formal proposal this temperature check became after gathering enough support.

compare.heading: What would another voting method have decided?
compare.intro: Votes are weighed today at 1 XRD = 1 vote: an account with 1,000 XRD has 1,000 votes. Here the same ballots are counted with other rules. Every voter keeps their choice and their XRD; only how much the vote weighs changes. It shows whether the result depends on the method and how centralised or decentralised power is under each one.
compare.kpi_consensus_all: Every method agrees with the current one: the result does not depend on the method
compare.kpi_consensus_hint: {changed} methods would have changed the result
compare.kpi_consensus_hint_one: 1 method would have changed the result
compare.kpi_current_hint: hold more than half of the vote, out of {total} voters
compare.kpi_spread_hint: {n} addresses needed to gather half of the vote ({pct} decentralisation)
compare.age_loading: Reading the age of each account on the ledger: {n} of {total}
compare.age_done: Age read on the ledger for all {total} accounts
compare.list_title: {n} ways to count the same votes

compare.detail_split: How the vote splits with this method
compare.detail_concentration: Who holds the weight of the vote
compare.detail_decisive: The {count} largest of the {of} addresses {side} (holding {xrd} XRD) were enough to decide it, even if everyone else had voted the other way.
compare.detail_nobody: No address meets this method's requirements, so there is no result.
compare.detail_no_quorum: The addresses that count under this method do not hold the XRD the quorum needs, so the result would not be valid and nobody got to decide it.
compare.g_nakamoto: Two measures of how spread power is. "Control 50 %" is the Nakamoto coefficient: the fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the weight. The degree of decentralisation is effective voters over voters (Simpson evenness, from the Herfindahl index): 100 % when all weigh the same. It takes every address into account and compares votes with few and many voters.
compare.g_decisive: How many addresses on the winning side, heaviest first, would have carried the result on their own even if everyone else had voted the other way.
compare.g_effective: How many voters there would be if they all weighed the same and power were just as centralised. If 150 accounts vote but amount to 10 effective voters, a few decide.
compare.g_age: Full years the account had been on the ledger when the vote opened: it is checked whether it already held something 1, 2 and 3 years earlier. Accounts migrated from Olympia count from the Babylon migration (September 2023).
compare.note_hypothetical: This is a simulation: real votes are counted at 1 XRD = 1 vote. The quorum is checked with the XRD of the addresses that count under each method; the approval threshold is the vote's own.
compare.note_pending: {n} recent votes have no voting power yet and are left out.
compare.note_unknown_age: The age of {n} accounts could not be read; age-based methods leave them out.
compare.empty: There are no weighed votes to compare yet.

linear.name: 1 XRD = 1 vote
linear.rule: Every XRD is a vote: 1,000 XRD weigh 1,000 votes. This is the method votes use today.
linear.attack: Splitting into addresses adds no votes. The only way to weigh more is to get more XRD, buying or borrowing it before the vote opens.

capped_10k.name: Capped at 10,000 XRD per address
capped_10k.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than 10,000 XRD: a very low cap that evens wallets out a lot.
capped_10k.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses of 10,000 XRD or less; in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote and it takes capital.

capped_100k.name: Capped at 100,000 XRD per address
capped_100k.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than 100,000 XRD.
capped_100k.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses of 100,000 XRD or less; in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote and it takes capital.

capped.name: Capped at 1,000,000 XRD per address
capped.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than {cap} XRD. It limits the largest wallets without taking their vote away.
capped.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses under {cap} XRD, so in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote: it takes capital.

capped_10m.name: Capped at 10,000,000 XRD per address
capped_10m.rule: Like today, but no address can weigh more than 10 million XRD: it only limits the largest whales.
capped_10m.attack: The cap is dodged by splitting the XRD into addresses of 10 million or less; in practice it is back to 1 XRD = 1 vote and it takes capital.

capped_share.name: Capped at {share} of the total
capped_share.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than {share} of all the XRD that voted. The cap grows with turnout.
capped_share.attack: Like the fixed cap: split across addresses, each part stays under {share} and counts in full.

capped_share_5.name: Capped at 5 % of the total
capped_share_5.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than 5 % of all the XRD that voted.
capped_share_5.attack: Split across addresses, each part stays under 5 % and counts in full: it takes capital.

capped_share_10.name: Capped at 10 % of the total
capped_share_10.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but no address can weigh more than 10 % of all the XRD that voted.
capped_share_10.attack: Split across addresses, each part stays under 10 % and counts in full: it takes capital.

quadratic.name: Quadratic voting
quadratic.rule: The vote weighs the square root of the balance: 100 XRD give 10 votes and 1,000,000 XRD give 1,000. Holding more still counts, but each extra XRD counts less.
quadratic.attack: Splitting multiplies the vote: 1,000,000 XRD in one address are worth 1,000 votes, but split into 1,000,000 addresses of 1 XRD they are worth 1,000,000.

cube_root.name: Cube root
cube_root.rule: The vote weighs the cube root of the balance: 1,000 XRD give 10 votes and 1,000,000 XRD give 100. It sits between quadratic and logarithmic voting.
cube_root.attack: Even more sensitive to splitting than quadratic: the smaller the parts, the more votes.

logarithmic.name: Logarithmic voting
logarithmic.rule: One vote is added each time the balance grows tenfold: 1,000 XRD give about 3 votes and 1,000,000 XRD about 6. The balance barely matters.
logarithmic.attack: An address with 1 XRD weighs almost as much as one with millions, so many small addresses multiply the vote.

tiered.name: Balance tiers
tiered.rule: 1 to 5 votes by balance: under 1,000 XRD, 1 vote; from 1,000, 2; from 10,000, 3; from 100,000, 4; from 1,000,000, 5.
tiered.attack: Any address with a balance has at least 1 vote: 1,000 addresses with 1 XRD outweigh one with 100 million.

one_address.name: 1 address = 1 vote
one_address.rule: Every address weighs the same, whatever it holds.
one_address.attack: New addresses are free and there is no KYC: one person can vote with as many addresses as they like, each holding just enough for the fee.

one_address_min.name: 1 address = 1 vote, from {min} XRD
one_address_min.rule: Only addresses holding at least {min} XRD count, and they all weigh the same.
one_address_min.attack: Each extra vote costs {min} XRD in a new address. Whoever has a lot of capital splits it across many addresses and gains a huge number of votes.

one_address_sybil.name: 1 address = 1 vote, sybil-resistant
one_address_sybil.rule: All weigh the same, but only addresses with at least {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count. Creating many new accounts does not help.
one_address_sybil.attack: New accounts do not count: it takes addresses set up over {years_sybil} year ago holding {balance} XRD each. Possible, but it has to be planned well ahead.

address_age.name: 1 address = 1 vote, plus 1 per year
address_age.rule: Each address has 1 vote, plus 1 extra vote for each full year of age. The balance does not matter; loyalty does.
address_age.attack: New addresses already have 1 vote, so creating many works just as with 1 address = 1 vote.

one_year.name: Accounts 1 year or older
one_year.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only accounts that were 1 year old or more when the vote opened count.
one_year.attack: Age belongs to the account, not to the XRD: freshly bought XRD can go into an account over a year old. Splitting gains nothing; it takes capital.

veterans.name: Veterans only ({years}+ years)
veterans.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only accounts that were {years} years old or more when the vote opened count.
veterans.attack: An account {years} or more years old is enough to hold XRD bought at the last minute. It leaves out newcomers, not buyers.

veterans_address.name: Veterans, 1 address = 1 vote
veterans_address.rule: Only accounts {years} years old or more count, and they all weigh the same.
veterans_address.attack: It takes many addresses created {years} or more years ago, even with a tiny balance. It cannot be improvised, but it is cheap for whoever prepared it.

veterans_bonus.name: Veterans with an age bonus
veterans_bonus.rule: Only accounts {years} years old or more count, and every full year adds {bonus} to the vote: 2 years weigh ×1.5 and 3 years ×1.75.
veterans_bonus.attack: Splitting gains nothing and the bonus belongs to the account, not to the XRD: in an old account, freshly bought XRD get the bonus too.

seniority_bonus.name: Age bonus for everyone
seniority_bonus.rule: Every account counts: 1 XRD = 1 vote, plus {bonus} for each full year of age.
seniority_bonus.attack: Splitting gains nothing; new accounts just get no bonus. It takes capital.

hybrid_half.name: Mixed 50 / 50
hybrid_half.rule: Half of the weight is shared by XRD and the other half equally between addresses.
hybrid_half.attack: Half of the weight is shared per address: with thousands of empty addresses, one person takes almost all of that half.

double_majority.name: Double majority
double_majority.rule: To pass it must clear the threshold twice: counting 1 XRD = 1 vote and counting 1 address = 1 vote. Like the European Union's qualified majority.
double_majority.attack: Passing takes capital and winning by addresses too, but blocking only takes empty addresses voting against.

quadratic_seniority.name: Quadratic with an age bonus
quadratic_seniority.rule: Square root of the balance, plus {bonus} for each full year of account age.
quadratic_seniority.attack: New addresses count (with no bonus), so splitting into many small addresses multiplies the vote as with quadratic voting.

sybil_quadratic.name: Sybil-resistant quadratic
sybil_quadratic.rule: Square root of the balance, but only addresses with at least {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age count.
sybil_quadratic.attack: Splitting multiplies the vote, but each address needs {balance} XRD and {years_sybil} year of age: the accounts have to be prepared ahead.

no_top1.name: Without the largest address
no_top1.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, leaving out the address with the most XRD. It shows whether a single wallet decides the result.
no_top1.attack: The exclusion is dodged by splitting the XRD into two addresses so neither is the largest. In the end it takes capital, as with 1 XRD = 1 vote.

no_whales.name: Without the {n} largest
no_whales.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, leaving out the {n} addresses with the most XRD. It shows whether the result hinges on a few wallets.
no_whales.attack: Whales dodge the exclusion by splitting their XRD into addresses smaller than the ten largest. It takes capital.

whales_only.name: Large wallets only
whales_only.rule: 1 XRD = 1 vote, but only addresses holding {whale} XRD or more count. It shows what the whales alone would have decided.
whales_only.attack: Only addresses holding {whale} XRD or more count; splitting gains nothing. It takes a lot of capital, though very few people decide.

tips.col_method: The rule deciding how much each vote weighs
tips.col_result: What this method would have decided, with the vote's quorum and approval threshold
tips.col_support: Weight in favour over weight in favour and against (abstentions left out). The vertical line marks the approval threshold
tips.col_counted: Addresses whose vote counts under this method; the rest are left out for not meeting its requirements
tips.col_nakamoto: The number is the fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the weight (Nakamoto coefficient). The level and the bar are the degree of decentralisation: effective voters over voters, 100 % when all weigh the same
tips.col_decisive: How many addresses on the winning side, heaviest first, would have been enough on their own to decide the vote, even if everyone else voted the other way
tips.outcome_approved: There is quorum and the vote in favour passes the approval threshold
tips.outcome_rejected: There is quorum, but the vote in favour does not reach the approval threshold
tips.outcome_no_quorum: The XRD of the addresses that count under this method fall short of the quorum, so the result would not be valid
tips.outcome_winner: The option with the most weight under this method
tips.outcome_none: No address meets this method's requirements
tips.support: {pct} in favour; at least {threshold} is needed
tips.nakamoto: {n} of {of} addresses ({share}) hold more than half of the weight. Degree of decentralisation: {spread}, as they amount to {eff} effective voters out of {of}: {level}
tips.counted: {n} addresses count; {out} are left out under this method
tips.decisive: The {count} largest of {of} addresses on the winning side, holding {xrd} XRD, were enough to decide it
tips.badge_current: The method votes use today: the others are compared with it
tips.badge_changes: Under this method the result would have differed from the current one
tips.badge_same: Under this method the result would have been the same as the current one
tips.conc_top1: The heaviest address holds {pct} of the vote
tips.conc_top10: The next 9 heaviest addresses hold {pct} of the vote
tips.conc_rest: All other addresses together hold {pct} of the vote
tips.detail_counted: Addresses whose vote counts under this method, and how many are left out
tips.detail_effective: Effective voters: {n} of {of}. It is the number of equally sized addresses that would share power the same way. If {of} addresses vote but amount to {n}, in practice about {n} wallets decide. It is 1 over the sum of each address's squared share of the weight (Herfindahl index). If all weighed the same it would be {of}
tips.detail_quorum: XRD of the addresses that count, against the minimum the vote needs for the result to be valid
tips.kpi_consensus: How many alternative methods would have given the same result as 1 XRD = 1 vote
tips.kpi_current: Under the current method, the fewest addresses that together hold more than half of the vote
tips.kpi_most_spread: The method with the highest degree of decentralisation
tips.kpi_most_concentrated: The method with the lowest degree of decentralisation: power sits in the fewest hands
tips.level_extreme: A single address holds more than half of the weight and decides alone, however many others vote
tips.level_high: Decentralisation below 15 %: power amounts to very few addresses
tips.detail_spread: Effective voters over voters (Simpson evenness). 100 % when every address weighs the same; the lower, the more weight sits with a few
tips.level_minimal: Decentralisation of 65 % or more: the weight is close to evenly shared
tips.col_resistance: Resistance to manipulation: how hard it is for one person to weigh more than their share. With no KYC, creating addresses and splitting XRD between them is free. Very low: gamed at almost no cost. High: weight only comes from buying XRD. Hover each method to see how it is gamed and what it would take to turn this vote around
tips.resistance_very_low: One person can multiply their vote by creating many addresses, at almost no cost
tips.resistance_low: Each extra vote is cheap, or the method's safeguard (a cap, an exclusion) is dodged for free by splitting the XRD across addresses
tips.resistance_medium: Gaming it takes accounts prepared long in advance, or it only works to block the result
tips.resistance_high: Splitting into addresses adds no votes: the only way to weigh more is to hold more XRD
tips.kpi_balanced: The method that best combines resistance to manipulation and decentralisation (geometric mean of both): hard to game and with power spread out. 100 % decentralisation means every address weighs the same
tips.kpi_unbalanced: The method that combines them worst: it fails at one of the two at least. A 100 % decentralised method (every address weighs the same) that can be gamed for free by creating addresses is not balanced
tips.fact_voters: Addresses whose vote the voting system has already weighed
tips.fact_xrd: Total voting power of those addresses under the current method
tips.fact_quorum: XRD that must take part for the result to be valid
tips.fact_threshold: Share of the vote in favour needed to pass
tips.counted_share: {pct} of the addresses that voted count under this method ({n} of {of}); the rest do not meet its requirements
tips.decisive_share: {pct} of the addresses on the winning side ({n} of {of}), heaviest first, were enough to decide the result even if everyone else voted the other way
tips.fact_option: {n} addresses voted "{label}" ({pct} of those who voted)

resistance_hints.very_low: votes multiply by creating addresses, almost for free
resistance_hints.low: extra votes are cheap or the safeguard is dodged by splitting
resistance_hints.medium: takes accounts prepared years ahead, or only works to block
resistance_hints.high: splitting gains nothing: only more XRD adds weight

compare.cost_addresses: To turn this vote around, {addresses} new addresses holding {each} XRD each would do ({xrd} XRD in total).
compare.cost_addresses_aged: To turn it around it would take {addresses} accounts at least {years} old holding {each} XRD each ({xrd} XRD in total). New accounts do not count.
compare.cost_capital: To turn it around it would take {xrd} more XRD ({pct} of what already voted).
compare.cost_capital_split: To turn it around it would take {xrd} more XRD ({pct} of what already voted), split across {addresses} addresses to dodge the cap.
compare.cost_capital_aged: To turn it around it would take {xrd} more XRD ({pct} of what already voted) held in an account at least {years} old; an old account with freshly bought XRD will do.
compare.cost_impossible: Adding votes cannot turn this result around.
compare.cost_none: There is no clear result to turn around (no quorum or no valid votes).
compare.g_resistance: How hard it is for one person to weigh more than their share. With no KYC, new addresses are free and so is splitting XRD between them, so methods that count addresses or favour small balances are easy to game. Each method's details price turning this vote around.
compare.kpi_balance_hint: {resistance} resistance · {n} of {of} addresses needed for half of the vote ({pct} decentralisation)
